done.why: I'd stashed every treasure I could find in the trophy case and reached 145 of 350 points. Every way out of the open area was blocked: the dam, the river ledge, two flooded passages, the hole under the altar, the Cyclops Room sign, the Canyon View rope, and the cave-ins. The egg wouldn't open, and I couldn't find any other treasures.

about: It's the white house and the Great Underground Empire, cut down to a pocket. You kill the troll, solve the echo in the Loud Room, rope down from the dome to the temple, and pray at the altar to get back out with the loot. Everything past that pocket is politely closed off: management signs, black water, a draught from the land of the dead. It's a treasure-hunting game where the edges of the map are part of the writing.

ending.what: No ending. I finished with 145/350 (Junior Adventurer) after banking the torch, platinum bar, sceptre, jeweled egg, gold coffin, painting and bag of coins.

moments.note: The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it behind me. Ominous.
I knocked the troll out with one blow and finished him with the next. Easier than I expected.
'Bar bar ...' Taking the bar just echoed back at me. Typing 'echo' changed the room's acoustics and then I could take it. A satisfying little puzzle.
Going east from Damp Cave put me on a ledge over the river with no boat. The first of a lot of closed edges.
The FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3 'closed for inspection' board was funny, and it was clearly a wall.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' The weight limit made me juggle items several times.
The score check said 64 already. It felt like real progress.
Praying at the altar sent me up to the forest, so I had a way out for my treasures.
I put out the candles and got 'It's really dark in here....' even though my lantern was on.
I'd carried the bell, book and candles all the way to the altar hole, and it turned me away with a lovely line. All that carrying for nothing.
The chimney fits 'you, a light to climb by and one thing more.' A clear rule, told in a nice way.
Found the skeleton with the coins and the key in the maze.
The Cyclops Room was closed with a sign and a snore 'like a rockslide.'
I got lost in the maze and dropped into a dead end I couldn't climb back out of. It took a dozen turns to find my way out.
'You have neither the tools nor the expertise.' The egg won't open, and nothing I found would open it.

wished: Open the jeweled egg. It looks like a treasure inside a treasure.
Get down the altar hole and use the bell, book and candles I carried all that way
Get a boat for the river below the Damp Cave ledge
Get into the dam, which seemed to be where the matches and other tools would be
Do something with the neatly sorted rubble heaps at the south cave-in

lines.why: Funny, and it told me straight away that the room itself was the puzzle.

lines.line: "FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management." You leave the dam to its inspection.
lines.why: A dry, in-world way of saying 'not this time.'

lines.line: You decide that whatever is down there has waited this long and can wait a little longer.
lines.why: The best-written of the closed doors, and also the most disappointing one, since I'd brought the exorcism kit.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It told me the exact carrying rule in a way that sounded like the place, not like a menu.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: Intriguing. It made me think something was hidden there. Nothing was.

fun.why: Collecting treasures and watching the score climb felt good, and the echo, praying at the altar and the chimney were all nice. The maze backtracking and the dead ends dragged a bit.

engagement.why: Checking the score kept me going after each deposit. I lost steam once I'd tried all the closed edges and nothing else turned up.

difficulty.why: The troll fell in two hits, and the puzzles were mostly familiar and light. The weight limit and the maze were the only real friction. That felt about right for a small area, maybe a little easy.

interestingness.why: The blocked-off edges were written with personality: the management signs, black water, sighing from the land of the dead. But the playable core is a small set of familiar puzzles, and several hints, like the rubble heaps and the insect crack, went nowhere.

prose.why: The new text was crisp and funny, and it sat well alongside the classic room descriptions. The dark-message slip at turn 100 was one small wobble.
